authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Choose another player. You both draw 1.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Proverbs 17:17 — “A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Hebrews 2:11 — “For which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: The first murder in history was fratricide: Cain killed Abel.
Jesus redefined family, calling those who do God's will His brothers.
Hebrew 'ach' implies blood ties or covenant loyalty.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: The immaterial part of a person; the animating force of life; the Holy Spirit.
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: Ethereal swirling wind and golden light forming a vague dove shape amidst chaotic waves, glowing atmosphere, divine presence, digital painting style
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Choose between Tower, Sheol, or Opponent's Hand. Reveal up 5 cards from the chosen location and take any number of them.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Job 33:4 — “The Spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: 2 Corinthians 3:6 — “...for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: Hebrew 'ruach' and Greek 'pneuma' both mean wind, breath, and spirit.
The Spirit is often symbolized by a dove, fire, wind, or water.
In the Old Testament, the Spirit empowered individuals for specific tasks; in the New, He indwells believers.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: One who guards, watches, protects, or maintains possession
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: A heavy, weathered iron key hanging from a hook on a rough stone wall next to a sturdy wooden door, illuminated by a single lantern
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Target player cannot Redeem cards until your next turn.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Psalm 121:5 — “The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: John 17:12 — “While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept...”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: Cain's deflective question 'Am I my brother's keeper?' is the first biblical use of the word.
The Psalms emphasize that the Keeper of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
In Acts, the keeper of the prison was converted after an earthquake opened the doors.
